reason: 13.9 inner-boundary symmetry under-specified: 'cylindrical symmetry' admits both the electric (polar/poloidal) and magnetic (axial/toroidal) axisymmetric sectors. The gold uses the MAGNETIC sector (reverse-engineered parities A_x=(+,-,+), A_y=(-,+,+), phi=(-,-,+); confirmed by 13.14 initializing a purely azimuthal E_phi field = magnetic-dipole / TE mode). Added a physics-level cue 'magnetic (axial) type - z-axis magnetic dipole / azimuthal toroidal vector potential' so a physicist derives the correct sector (phi odd in x,y; A_x~-y, A_y~x) instead of the naive electric/polar default (what pro chose). No parity table given (kept derivable). Prompt-only; targets unchanged. CAVEAT: A_z slot is physically zero in this sector but the unit test feeds nonzero A_z - not addressed by this edit.

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import simpson as simps
after:
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import simps
reason: Remove a smuggled-in library-version workaround: R3 had silently rewritten the upstream dependency 'from scipy.integrate import simps' to 'from scipy.integrate import simpson as simps' to survive scipy>=1.14 (which dropped integrate.simps->simpson). That edit (a) was un-laddered and (b) bakes a version hack into the benchmark data. With multi-environment OR grading now handling library drift (a pre-1.14 'era' env in the OR set resolves simps), the data should be faithful to the original SciCode problem; reverted to the exact upstream dependency string. Sole such workaround in the dataset (verified: full required_dependencies diff vs upstream + API-token field sweep across all 65 problems => only #28). Consequence: problem 28 now passes only in an env exposing scipy.integrate.simps (scipy<1.14), which is exactly what the OR set's 2024-era env provides. Targets/h5 unaffected (deps-only change).
